questions.question: 1. Wollaston Prism are also known as

explanations.a: This is the correct option. A Wollaston prism, commonly used in differential interference contrast (DIC) microscopy, is an optical device that splits a light beam into two polarized rays and is often called a Nomarski prism when modified for DIC.
explanations.b: This is an incorrect option because a Wollaston prism is not hollow.
explanations.c: This is an incorrect option because a Wollaston prism does not absorb light.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect option because a Wollaston prism does not scatter light.

questions.question: 2. In which microscopy, unscattered light is blocked

explanations.a: This is an incorrect option because in bright field microscopy, the unscattered light passes through the sample and enters the objective.
explanations.b: This is an incorrect option because, like bright field microscopy, light field microscopy allows unscattered light to pass through the sample to form the image.
explanations.c: This is the correct option. In dark field microscopy, the directly transmitted or unscattered light is blocked, so only light scattered by edges, defects, or surface features reaches the objective.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect option because in dark field microscopy, unscattered light is specifically blocked to create a dark background and highlight scattered light from defects or edges.

questions.question: 3. Which microscopy uses material's birefringence to increase contrast and expose structural and textural details

explanations.a: This is an incorrect option because dark field microscopy relies on scattered light from edges, defects, or surface features to form an image, not on the material’s birefringence.
explanations.b: This is an incorrect option because bright field microscopy forms images primarily through variations in light absorption or transmission.
explanations.c: This is the correct option. Polarised light microscopy exploits the birefringence of anisotropic materials to enhance contrast and reveal structural, textural, and crystallographic details.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect option because only polarised light microscopy uses birefringence to enhance contrast and reveal structural or textural details.

questions.question: 4. Which of the following microstructural features is typically visible under bright field optical microscopy in metals?

explanations.a: This is an incorrect option because electron band structure is a quantum mechanical property of materials at the atomic scale.
explanations.b: This is the correct option. Bright field optical microscopy can resolve features at the micrometer scale, such as grain boundaries, phases, and inclusions in metals.
explanations.c: This is an incorrect option because dislocation loops are nanometer-scale defects within the crystal lattice.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect option because atomic lattice spacing occurs at the angstrom (Å) scale, far below the resolving power of an optical microscope.

questions.question: 5. Compared to bright field microscopy, dark field imaging provides:

answers.b: Better visualization of fine surface details

explanations.a: This is an incorrect option because dark field microscopy has similar optical resolution to bright field, and the contrast of fine features is actually enhanced, not reduced.
explanations.b: This is the correct option. Dark field microscopy blocks unscattered light and collects only light scattered by edges, defects, or surface features.
explanations.c: This is an incorrect option because dark field significantly improves visibility of small or scattered features compared to bright field.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect option because dark field microscopy produces bright features on a dark background, and the image can be colored if using color-sensitive detectors or filters; it is not inherently limited to grayscale.

questions.question: 6. In metallography, dark field microscopy is particularly useful for detecting:

explanations.a: This is an incorrect option because tracking grain boundary migration requires time-lapse imaging or high-resolution methods, not standard dark field microscopy.
explanations.b: This is an incorrect option because atomic lattice features are far below the optical resolution limit; TEM or HRTEM is needed.
explanations.c: This is the correct option. Dark field microscopy enhances contrast by collecting scattered light, making it ideal for visualizing small defects, inclusions, or precipitates on or near the surface.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect option because magnetic domains are not visible via scattered light
